method: Fresh bounded complete-yod and full-word comparison at six remaining BEL dagesh sites. Original A2 lower-Theodotion pixels only, native crops and integer nearest-neighbor enlargement. Pointed/plain WIS pairs, a clear same-page narrow-neck pointed Daniel40, four literal same-page plain yods and independently certified SUS27/47 yods establish added low-left-node morphology. Three targets retain inset white windows; verse42 has a fully bridged but complete matching added-node contour. Physical connectivity alone neither disqualifies a surviving diagnostic point nor proves a point in an opaque swollen body. Both unsupported saturated sites retain notes. No OCR, expected spelling, grammar, modern vocalization, enhancement or unproven new-scan independence supplies a mark. Seven original PDF page images were freshly extracted and all70 durable images exactly replayed. Six old scratch locator crops, some clipping letter tops, are explicitly excluded from the evidence packet.

accepted.finding: A compact rounded low-left lobe survives below the tapered yod head, joined to the ordinary descending right leg while retaining a small inset white window. The same added-node contour appears in literal pointed WIS8:3/13:10 and same-page Daniel40 controls; plain local yods terminate in a single narrow right leg without that lobe. The high side-node position is above the separate vowel line. Complete word and lower-Theodotion source continuation establish the addressed yod.

The full yod retains a rounded low-left added node, small white notch/window under the head and a separate continuing right-leg outline. It repeats the same-font pointed yod morphology and differs from four plain same-page yod footprints, which have no low-left bulb. The already printed patah remains below the letter and is not part of the side node.

The extra low-left rounded node surrounds a small white window beneath the tapered head while the original narrow right leg continues below it. Same-page narrow-neck pointed Daniel40 and literal WIS pointed/plain pairs locate this as an added side point; four plain local yods lack the lower-left bulb. The existing holam above remains unchanged.

The yod has a compact rounded lower-left node beneath an inset left edge of the head, plus the ordinary continuing right leg. Its fully bridged node has no enclosed white window, but the complete contour repeats independently certified SUS27/47 pointed yods and agrees with the narrower same-page Daniel40 point. Four literal plain yod bodies have only a single thin right leg and lack this added node. The complete morphology, rather than physical separation alone, certifies the side point.
